decisions.decision: Use code 106 (accessory lot with an improvement, e.g. a detached garage on a split-off lot) will be assigned one ERU.
A property with multiple houses/units but only one line item and one tax bill in the assessor's spreadsheet will be charged one ERU, matched to the tax bill rather than the number of dwellings.

The Carousel Lane / Emerald Place condominium complex, owned by a single LLC, will be billed as one combined property using Weston & Samson's total-property ERU estimate rather than per individual unit.
The Lunenburg Housing Authority property on White Street is flagged as a likely exception (a government entity that would effectively be taxing itself), pending further review.
Members will each review the mass use code document and John's assigned ERU-per-use-code list, and send back any disagreements before the next meeting so John can revise the model.
Next meeting tentatively set for June 24 (a Wednesday), with June 29 as a fallback if that date does not work for everyone, pending confirmation with Tim and Mark.

The task force agreed it should revisit its own officer and liaison assignments (chair, vice chair, board representatives) now that town elections have occurred, though this was deferred rather than acted on.

minutes.headline: Task force is assigning stormwater ERU fees property-by-property, leaning toward per-ERU billing over flat tiers
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed John's detailed matching of the assessor's full property list against Weston & Samson's impervious-area survey, working through Massachusetts use codes one by one to assign a baseline ERU (equivalent residential unit) and resulting fee to every property in town, including tricky cases like garage-only lots, duplexes, condo complexes, and the Housing Authority. No formal vote was taken on the methodology; the group reached working consensus on several categories, assigned homework to review the rest before the next meeting, and discussed presenting both an operating-budget and a stand-alone-utility funding option to voters at the fall special town meeting.

what_happened.line: The task force decided to bill the Carousel Lane/Emerald Place condo complex as one combined property rather than unit by unit.
The Lunenburg Housing Authority's White Street property was flagged as a likely exception, since billing it would mean the town taxing itself.

Members discussed presenting voters two funding options at the fall special town meeting: folding the fee into the operating budget, where it would rise with the annual levy, or a stand-alone utility fee.
Working consensus was reached on ERU assignments for several property categories, including accessory lots and multi-unit parcels billed on one tax bill.
No formal vote was taken on the methodology; members got homework to review the ERU list before the next meeting, tentatively June 24.

why_it_matters: Every property in town, including condos, duplexes and multi-house lots, is being assigned a stormwater fee based on impervious surface, which will eventually appear on a bill.
Voters will be asked at the fall special town meeting to choose how the stormwater program is funded, a choice that affects whether the fee rises automatically with the town's annual tax levy.
Owners of shared or multi-unit properties should watch how their property is classified, since billing decisions are being made property-by-property rather than unit-by-unit.
